sub_rqs.question: How does the adoption of AI and machine learning anomaly detection by auditors affect external audit quality, such as misstatement and fraud detection, restatements, and discretionary accruals?
sub_rqs.rationale: This is the core dependent variable of the topic: the direct effect of AI-based detection on audit quality.
queries: artificial intelligence adoption audit quality
audit data analytics audit quality restatements
machine learning auditing misstatement detection
technology-enabled auditing fraud detection effectiveness

sub_rqs.question: How does the use of AI and audit analytics affect audit fees, audit hours and effort, and audit efficiency?
sub_rqs.rationale: This addresses the second dependent variable, audit costs, and whether efficiency gains are passed on to clients.
queries: audit analytics audit fees effect
artificial intelligence audit efficiency audit hours
big data analytics audit cost reduction
audit fee audit effort technology investment

sub_rqs.question: How accurate and effective are machine learning and anomaly detection techniques at identifying fraudulent transactions and anomalous journal entries in audit settings?
sub_rqs.rationale: The technical performance of the tools underlies any quality effect and must be understood before interpreting the audit outcomes.
queries: journal entry testing machine learning anomaly detection
financial statement fraud detection machine learning
unsupervised anomaly detection accounting transactions audit
deep learning fraudulent journal entries autoencoder

sub_rqs.question: Through which mechanisms and under which conditions (auditor judgment, skepticism, client complexity, firm size, regulation) does AI-based detection change audit outcomes?
sub_rqs.rationale: Mechanisms and moderators explain why effects on quality and cost vary across engagements and firms.
queries: auditor judgment reliance on AI tools
professional skepticism audit data analytics
audit firm size technology adoption audit outcomes
algorithm aversion auditors decision support

sub_rqs.question: What are the adoption drivers, implementation barriers, and risks (false positives, explainability, data quality, liability, regulatory concerns) of AI in external auditing?
sub_rqs.rationale: Adoption conditions and unintended effects determine whether quality and cost benefits are realized in practice.
queries: barriers to artificial intelligence adoption in auditing
explainable AI audit risks false positives
continuous auditing machine learning implementation challenges
regulatory standards AI audit evidence PCAOB

search_strategy: Cover roughly 2010 to the present, with emphasis on 2016 onward when audit analytics and machine learning adoption accelerated. Prefer archival and empirical studies, experiments, field studies, and systematic reviews in accounting, auditing, and information systems, plus technical fraud detection papers from arXiv for rq3. Exclude papers on internal fraud detection in banking or payments with no audit link, and purely opinion or vendor pieces. The thinnest literature is expected for rq2 (causal evidence on audit fees and costs from AI specifically) and for direct archival evidence on AI and audit quality in rq1.
